data.title: 'Complex' world of Taliban home: Wife embraces Taliban 'brothers', asserts women's right to freedom
data.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Elise Blanchard, award-winning photojournalist and author of “Dans la Maison d’un Taliban” (In the House of a Taliban). Blanchard’s work challenges narratives that reduce Afghan women to passive victims. Drawing on rare access to a Taliban household, she describes a social landscape shaped by profound contradictions. In drought-stricken Badghis province, Blanchard traces child marriage through a chain of material pressures exacerbated by climate change. Gendered violence is explained through the prism of patriarchy, poverty, drought and political instability.

data.title: Iceland rejects EU accession talks

data.title: ‘Everything’s smashed to bits’: Ukrainians turn anger on those storing weapons near their villages
data.description: As Russia hits another ammunition warehouse, killing at least 38, locals put blame on poorly placed depots It is a day and a half since a Russian jet-powered drone smashed into an ammunition dump in Myla , a village 15 miles outside central Kyiv. Volodymyr, 61, a security guard, leads visitors from his family’s badly damaged home, its roof blown off, back windows shattered, through the garden towards the impact site 300 metres away. The garden, like so many in Ukraine’s villages and suburbs, is a sizeable allotment. But today the greenhouse is shattered, a vegetable patch is blackened and crisp underfoot. Several metres of grapevine have been destroyed. Even so, Volodymyr finds two surviving bunches to hand to the Guardian. Continue reading...

data.title: Forbidden planet: was Pluto’s 2006 demotion a big mistake?
data.description: Since it was stripped of planetary status, Pluto’s defenders have been fighting the decision – and they’re only getting more passionate Twenty years ago, Pluto got demoted. After a vote by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in August 2006, Pluto was relegated from major planet to dwarf planet status. Our solar system dropped from nine planets to eight. At the time, many scientists were unhappy with the decision. Two decades on, the debate is, if anything, even more polarised. “The definition of a planet they created, you can’t use it at all,” says Philip Metzger, the director of the Stephen W Hawking Centre for Microgravity Research and Education at the University of Central Florida. “It makes the definition of a planet completely non-useful in science.” Continue reading...

data.title: I’m giving birth as a battle rages over maternity care in Ireland. We shouldn’t have to pay to feel safe | Caelainn Hogan
data.description: An unfair two-tier system is, at last, giving way to universal state care. But private interests and highly paid doctors are resisting There were no chandeliers in the public ward where I spent my first days as a mother, at the oldest continuously operating maternity hospital in the world. The room echoed with cries, the well-worn floor bouncing under footsteps, the windows looking out on Dublin’s city centre. Now the Rotunda hospital, where I’m due to give birth again soon, is counting down to its 1 millionth baby. It is also at the centre of a bitter debate over plans to reform Ireland’s two-tier state healthcare system, so that those who pay to “go private” in public hospitals no longer gain an unfair advantage over those who don’t. Caelainn Hogan is a journalist and the author of Republic of Shame: How Ireland Punished ‘Fallen Women’ and Their Children Continue reading...

data.title: Is it true that … mental health is affected by inflammation?
data.description: Studies have found that anti-inflammatory drugs can improve your mood. But what does that mean for conditions such as depression and anxiety? Inflammation is the immune system’s response to injury or infection. If you cut yourself and the area becomes red and swollen, that’s inflammation: immune cells are rushing to fight germs and repair tissue. But inflammation can also occur in the body during illnesses, and a low level of inflammation can arise from obesity or ageing. “A marker of that inflammation tends to be elevated cytokines in people’s blood,” says Prof Daniel M Davis, head of life sciences at Imperial College London and author of Immune Health: A Myth-Busting Guide . “They’re the molecules immune cells use to communicate with each other.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Breakthrough’ as Turkmenistan starts fixing ‘mindboggling’ methane mega-leaks
data.description: Secretive state begins repairs on ageing facilities after being revealed as worst country for leaks of potent greenhouse gas Turkmenistan has started plugging the mega-leaks of methane that spew from its ageing oil and gas facilities, the latest UN data shows, in a move hailed as a breakthrough. Methane, also called natural or fossil gas, is a potent greenhouse gas. It traps 80 times more heat than carbon dioxide and causes 25% of global heating today. Stopping leaks can be quick and cheap and, because methane breaks down in the atmosphere far quicker than CO2, this has a rapid impact, with some experts calling it the climate “emergency brake”. Continue reading...

data.title: The one change that worked: I stopped listening to podcasts – and my mind flooded with ideas
data.description: For decades my life was soundtracked by comedy duos, mostly male, discussing their friendships. When I gave them up, I felt as if I was having a mental reboot I have always loved podcasts. The genre of audio I have come to think of as Two Men Talking (In Excessive Detail About Their Lives) has been one of my favourite forms of entertainment for decades. It started with a semi-religious devotion to a Sunday morning XFM show hosted by Jimmy Carr and the comedy writer Iain Morris, but as the years progressed and podcasting boomed, I was soon spoilt for choice. Eventually there were enough comedy duos candidly discussing their hopes, fears and awkward social interactions to fill every moment of my day. data.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Jerry, the king of dogs, who taught me how to live
data.description: After a burglary, my parents decided we needed extra security. Jerry was the answer – and this hungry, handsome hound helped us all in countless ways Jerry came into our lives because a burglar had broken in. My mum had woken in the middle of the night to find an intruder in our kitchen. He scarpered, but the psychological damage was done. Two days later, my dad came home with the cutest little rescue puppy, with traces of beagle and labrador in him. He was two months old, had a black, brown and white coat, and big, bashful eyes. We called him Jerry because we had a cat called Tom. “I’m not sure how he’ll protect us,” I said. “He will,” my dad replied. Jerry was very laid-back and Zen. He became part of the family straight away. He also became the therapy dog we hadn’t realised we needed. With two teenagers in the house (me and my older brother) and a hyperactive younger brother, someone was always in a strop and needing to let off steam by taking him out for a walk. Each time, Jerry obliged. I’d bore him with my latest teen-romance trauma; he was a very good listener. Sometimes, he’d have five walks a day, with both of my parents taking their turn. He certainly got his steps in. Continue reading...

data.description: Forget writing that novel: the most satisfying tasks are often the smallest. From batch cooking and bird feeding, to filling a kettle with meticulous precision, our readers reveal their favourites Sometimes, it’s the smallest accomplishments that bring the biggest feelings of joy. You don’t need to run a marathon or write a novel to get a sense of achievement; something as simple as reorganising your cutlery drawer or repairing a garden fence can prove surprisingly satisfying. Here, readers share the modest achievements that have brought them great pleasure. I really enjoy cooking and have a large collection of spices. Recently, I bought a few dozen glass bottles and organised my herbs and spices in a drawer, with labels on the lids and sides. Every time I cook, I feel pleasure from being able to instantly put my hand on the requisite spice without fumbling through piles of little boxes, and having to open and smell them to be sure which is which. data.title: ‘Sometimes you just need a good cry’: why Little Women is my feelgood movie
data.description: The latest in our series of writers highlighting their go-to comfort films is an ode to the teary 1994 adaptation of the classic novel I have an ongoing argument with some friends about how I refuse to watch Interstellar again, despite considering it a beautiful and well-crafted film. It’s just so sad, I tell them, even with its hopeful ending. A desperate, choking lump forms in my chest as soon as I hear the futuristic swells of Hans Zimmer’s score and I have to remove myself before I am overtaken by emotion. But at the same time, the movie I choose as my feelgood film is one that has reduced me to a sobbing, snotty mess time and time again, whether I’m watching it curled up with my cat on the couch, swaddled in blankets while sick in bed or jostling with my seatmate for the armrest on an airplane. And just like with the score from Interstellar, the moment I hear Thomas Newman’s wistful little oboe intro of the 1994 version of Little Women, I can feel my eyes well up with tears. Continue reading...

data.title: The Nepal floods seem a world away – but make no mistake, climate breakdown will affect us all | Nesrine Malik
data.description: Richer countries might have more resources to deal with catastrophe, but this problem grips the entire planet, however much leaders may want to deny it Climate breakdown is happening on one Earth, but two different worlds. In one, its impacts increasingly encroach on everyday life; longer periods of discomfort and shorter periods of sharp pain. Endless, hotter summers, and within them sudden wildfires, evacuations, homes burned to cinders in a matter of hours. In another, catastrophe. This summer has been a snapshot of that split-screen. The hottest day on record in parts of Europe, and a wave of water, mud and ice in Nepal that so far has claimed more than 750 lives. Thousands of people are still missing. The difference is also one of resources. The climate crisis has an economic cost, but some places can absorb it better than others. Responses to this summer of wildfires in Europe included a rapid scrambling by the French government to provide everything from tax breaks for businesses affected by the fires to relocation costs and aid to rebuild homes . The UK government had deployed almost £100m before the summer to strengthen wildfire resilience. Continue reading...

data.title: Space junk punched a new hole in the moon. It’s not ours to abuse | Moriba Jah
data.description: The space industry treats the sky as a place to dump what it no longer wants. We must develop a new model of accountability On 5 August, a piece of a derelict SpaceX rocket traveling at 5,400 miles an hour met with the moon and punched a fresh hole into it near Einstein Crater . Astronomers were thrilled. The European Southern Observatory caught sodium and lithium flaring in the debris plume and called it a bonus. The media called it a light show. Nobody was physically hurt, so nobody is responsible, and within a week the story was gone. I have spent 20 years tracking the junk humanity leaves behind in space for a living, and I want to tell you plainly what that crater actually is: a receipt. It’s what you get when an entire industry treats the sky, and now the moon, as a place to dump what it no longer wants, and calls the dumping “normal operations” or “space exploration”. Continue reading...

data.title: Do you have a bespoke ‘dirty zone’? | Emma Beddington
data.description: Apparently a dedicated mud room will make you less stressed. But I have a very different approach I was excited to learn that the latest interiors essential, according to the Washington Post , is a “dirty zone”. I’m ahead of the curve – I’ve already got a dirty zone by each main door (and also one directly outside the back door, where, rudely, a mystery animal has defecated). The fridge drawers are dirty zones thanks to the windfall apples I thought I would cook, but predictably left to liquefy. There’s a dirty zone next to the washing machine and a mildewy one inside it. There’s the festering compost bin I’m too chicken to tackle post-heatwave, plus the cupboard under the stairs, which we don’t talk about. Good luck finding a clean zone, basically. Does this make me kinda chic ? Unfortunately not: the Post is actually preaching the benefits of confining the sordid ephemera of life to carefully delineated and hidden areas: storage benches, monogrammed totes or even a “mud room” (for coats, shoes, skis, lacrosse sticks and dog-washing sinks – I think posh Britons call it a boot room). A 2021 study in the Netherlands found that participants who did chores in chaotic environments had higher levels of the stress marker salivary alpha-amylase. I always wonder what’s brewing in my mouth as I fall over piles of filthy shoes yet again while running to answer the door. Continue reading...

data.title: OnlyFans and AI training: why gen Z doesn’t care where our money comes from | Alice Lassman
data.description: With traditional goals such as stability and homeownership feeling out of reach, young people are focused on the present By now, we all know the shape of financial nihilism: the throw-your-money-at-anything reaction to the dissolution of the slow, linear path to wealth; the prediction markets , meme stocks , cryptocurrencies and microluxuries growing in its place. We’re left in an economic no man’s land. But financial nihilism only describes where we put our money. What about how we earn it in the first place? The modern economy has long relied on our need for stable employment – to pay the mortgage, to keep our kids fed, or, for some, to chase prestige and power – to generate the work ethic that keeps the wheel of production turning. None of this is going well for young people. Our jobs are insecure , we can’t afford houses, we’re deferring having kids (if we have them at all), and only 6% of us say a leadership position is our primary career goal. Hope is one of the economy’s most productive inputs, powering our willingness to endure long hours. When the production function of income – the mechanism that turns hard work into a stable salary, then a mortgage, then a pension – breaks down, so does our relationship with the input. I call this production nihilism: my generation’s growing indifference to the kinds of work we’re willing to participate in, and where we’re willing to earn. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump’s plan to sell off a part of Yosemite is what oligarchy looks like | Rebecca Solnit
data.description: Public lands belong to all of us. Noone should plunder those lands for profit Do people still say a car was “sold for parts”? Because the US is being sold for parts or just handed over to the oligarchy. It’s a fire sale, a bankruptcy auction, it’s a planned dismantling of everything from its military to its institutions of higher education to its scientific research to its public lands. And while the threat to sell off part of Yosemite National Park is about a quarter-mile parcel on the park’s edge, Yosemite is a crown jewel in the national park system and, arguably, the world’s first national park. Rebecca Solnit is a Guardian US columnist. She is the author of Orwell’s Roses and co-editor with Thelma Young Lutunatabua of the climate anthology Not Too Late: Changing the Climate Story from Despair to Possibility Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the rise of Germany’s AfD: mainstream parties must deliver a bolder response | Editorial
data.description: The far right is close to winning a state election for the first time since the second world war. A different economic approach is needed to combat it The early autumn has become a time of foreboding and angst in German politics. In the eastern states that have become strongholds for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party, it has regularly made headline-grabbing advances in September elections. Only the refusal of mainstream politicians to form coalitions with one of Europe’s most extreme movements has kept it out of power. This year, the lights are flashing red. Next weekend, when voters in Saxony-Anhalt cast their ballots, the signs are that the traditional firewall may not be enough. In polling, the AfD is currently scoring above 40% in the state, which could win it enough seats to govern on its own. Compared with the last election in 2021, its support has doubled; backing for the closest challenger, the centre-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU), has tumbled by almost 15%. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on rare earths: it’s common sense to secure essential supply chains | Editorial
data.description: Outsourcing the industry to China cannot continue, but Europe knows it can no longer count on the US for a solution The alarm sounded 16 years ago. In 2010, China blocked exports of key rare earths to Japan in a row over disputed islands in the East China Sea. The critical minerals are essential to everything from advanced weaponry and iPhones to electric vehicle batteries and wind turbines, so the rest of the world took note. But it didn’t take much action. China still accounts for about 70% of rare-earth mining globally and 90% of separation and processing. Then, last year, Beijing forced Donald Trump to back away from his trade war – not with its retaliatory tariffs, but the curbing of rare-earth exports. A scramble for new supplies began in earnest. The year-long trade truce is due to expire in November. The price of erbium, an element essential to communications infrastructure, has already jumped because of fears that export controls will soon be renewed. Continue reading...

data.title: Venus Williams bows out after 2am following latest start in US Open history
data.description: Kenin wins 6-2, 7-6 (6) in late-night contest Williams loses 15th straight tour-level match First-round clash finally begins at 12.13am Sunday had become Monday by the time Venus Williams finally emerged beneath the closed roof of Arthur Ashe Stadium, her entrance pushed deep into the night after Novak Djokovic’s bruising defeat by Argentina’s Mariano Navone went the five-set distance. The first ball was struck at 12.13am, the latest start to a match in US Open history, yet several thousand spectators remained to watch a player who has been part of this tournament for as long as the building itself. At 46 years old, ranked 611th in the world and making her record-extending 26th US Open singles appearance, Williams has grown accustomed to making history simply by showing up. Even by those standards this latest installment was, as she would later describe it, “completely insane”. Continue reading...

data.title: Aston Villa and Chelsea still enemies despite transfer pipeline, insists Emery

data.title: Marcus Rashford’s Manchester United return feels like a marriage of convenience | Will Unwin
data.description: A lack of offers and problems in finding a replacement may be behind the move, but that does not mean it cannot work The first chant of the match was for Marcus Rashford, Manchester United’s returning rogue son, the one banished for 18 months, first to the Midlands and then Catalonia. Every football fan loves an academy product who has risen up the ranks, from scrawny child to getting 76,000 off their seats. Rashford is one of these, living out the dream of everyone inside Old Trafford and they are willing to forgive but want something in return. Not since 7 December 2024 has Rashford been seen in red at Old Trafford. Then it was as a substitute forlornly trying to turn things around in an eventual 3-2 defeat by Nottingham Forest. His relationship with Ruben Amorim was already deteriorating, the second head coach to have become irritated with Rashford. After loans with Aston Villa and Barcelona, everyone is surprised to see him back; it feels like a marriage of convenience because of a lack of offers and securing a replacement was deemed complex. Continue reading...

data.title: Mikel Arteta ‘begging’ Premier League to expand 20-man matchday squads
data.description: Arsenal manager says dropping players ‘affects wellbeing’ Serie A allows 25-player matchday squads and La Liga 23 Arsenal have asked the Premier League to increase the size of matchday squads, with Mikel Arteta saying the current system is detrimental to player welfare. Top‑flight clubs can name 20 players for games, including a minimum of three homegrown players. In Spain’s La Liga, clubs can name a matchday squad of 23, while Italy’s Serie A allows 25. Arsenal have competed on multiple fronts in recent seasons. Last year, as well as winning the Premier League, they reached the finals of the Champions League and Carabao Cup , as well as the quarter-finals of the FA Cup. With pressure increasing on the football calendar and players facing more matches, Arteta sees no reason why English teams should operate with smaller squads than those from other European leagues. data.title: All-time great Aaron Donald comes out of retirement to rejoin stacked LA Rams
data.description: Los Angeles were already Super Bowl favorites Defensive tackle was 10-time Pro Bowler with Rams 35-year-old aiming to win second Super Bowl in LA Aaron Donald, one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history , is coming out of retirement to rejoin his only professional team, the Los Angeles Rams. During a 10-season career with the Rams, who drafted him with the 13th overall pick in 2014, Donald was a three-time defensive player of the year and an eight-time first team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl with the Rams at the end of the 2021 season before announcing his retirement in March 2024 at the age of 32. Continue reading...

data.title: Bhutan hosts first ‘conscious food summit’ amid threats to global supplies
data.description: Organisers say people must revive spiritual relationship with food amid double threat of climate crisis and conflict Mending the broken food system under the threat of climate-driven weather extremes will require more than economic fixes and intensive agriculture, according to the organisers of a pioneering summit this week, who say the world must revive its spiritual relationship with food. Delegates from more than 60 countries and the UN will gather for the next five days in Paro in the tiny Himalayan nation of Bhutan for the world’s first “conscious food summit”, which will bring together governments and farmers, mindfulness experts and yoga therapists. data.title: Weather tracker: Warm Yellow Sea strengthens storms in South Korea
data.description: More than 200mm of rain forecast in parts of South Korea, while parts of southern Europe to be 10C above average South Korea’s prime minister, Han Seong-sook, met officials to prepare for heavy rain expected this week, with rainfall totals across central and northern parts of the country forecast to exceed 200mm in some areas. South Korea was battered by heavy rainfall earlier this month and some areas were particularly hard hit. Over the weekend further thunderstorms pushed into the region and these are expected to cause disruption through Monday. This heavy rain is caused by a series of severe thunderstorms that developed over the Yellow Sea, on the western side of South Korea, and will slowly push eastwards on Monday before easing on Tuesday. These storms have been strengthened by the very warm Yellow Sea, which now has a surface temperature of 29C, 4C above the climatological average. Continue reading...

data.title: UK households will take £2,400 financial hit from Iran war, analysis shows
data.description: Centre for Economics and Business Research calculates effect of inflation and wage stagnation to end of 2027 UK households will have suffered a £2,400 financial hit, on average, from the Iran war by the end of 2027, new analysis shows. The Centre for Economics and Business Research (CEBR) has calculated that the jump in inflation since the conflict began, and weaker wage growth, will knock £1,100 off the real income of the average UK household in 2026, and by a further £1,300 in 2027. data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russia planning ‘massive strikes’ on power plants days after its deadliest attack of the year
data.description: Russia’s defence ministry preparing attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure as death toll from warehouse strike rises to 38. What we know on day 1,650 Russia’s defence ministry says it is gearing up for large-scale attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in a tit-for-tat response to strikes by Kyiv. “Russian forces have begun preparations for massive strikes against facilities in Ukraine’s energy sector in response to the ongoing attacks by the Kyiv regime on civilian infrastructure and on Russia’s oil and energy complex,” it said on Telegram on Sunday. Last winter, Moscow repeatedly hit Ukrainian power plants, devastating the country’s energy sector and plunging millions of people into cold and darkness in sub-zero temperatures. In comes as the death toll from a Russian strike on a warehouse west of Kyiv rose to 38 , with four people still missing , making it the deadliest attack of the year , Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said on Sunday. The Friday night strike on the warehouse, which Ukrainian officials said was storing ammunition, sparked massive explosions and fires that swept through dozens of nearby homes and buildings in the village of Myla. Russian strikes on Kyiv on Saturday killed a 2-year-old girl and injured 12 others, the capital’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said. In the village of Bilbasovka in eastern Ukraine, a 13-year-old and an adult died after Russian troops dropped bombs on private houses on Sunday, according to local official Vadim Lyakh. Meanwhile, a ⁠missile attack killed two ⁠people and ⁠injured another ​16 in the Russian ⁠city of Belgorod, close ⁠to the ​border ‌with ‌ Ukraine , on ‌Sunday evening, the acting governor, Alexander Shuvayev, said on ‌Telegram. He said two ​people were killed after Ukraine hit ⁠a commercial facility, ​with the ​attack ​also causing ​fires ‌in ​seven ​warehouses in the city. Another ⁠person ⁠was ​killed ⁠in a Ukrainian ​attack ‌on ‌a mine ‌in the Russian-controlled ‌part of the Luhansk ​region ⁠in ​eastern Ukraine, ​the ​region’s Russian-installed ​governor, ‌Leonid ​Pasechnik, ​said. Ukraine wants ⁠to bring forward part of ⁠a European ⁠Union ​loan earmarked for next year ⁠to help cover a $27bn budget ⁠deficit this year, ​said its defence ‌minister, Yevhenii Khmara. In comments to ‌reporters released on Sunday, he added that Kyiv’s war plan must be ‌clear to Ukraine’s partners, as well ​as across the military chain of command. Khmara also said ⁠Ukraine has tested ​four ​potential interceptors to ​shoot down the ​jet-powered ‌drones ​Russia ​is increasingly firing at Ukraine . Swarms of the high-speed drones have plagued the capital Kyiv for four consecutive days, killing residents, damaging homes and warehouses and upending daily life. Ukraine ⁠is preparing for further talks ⁠with ⁠representatives of ​the US president, Donald Trump, Zelenskyy said on ⁠Sunday. “There will ​be ‌more details ‌tomorrow. We ‌will do everything we can so that war does not remain ‌the only option for ​how events unfold further. It is important that ⁠America shares ​many of our ​views on ​the situation,” ​he ‌said ​in ​a televised statement. A Nato official said on Sunday Russia is stepping up hybrid ⁠acts in Europe, but that at this time the alliance sees no imminent threat ⁠of attack. “Even as ⁠the ​Russians are facing very substantial resistance from Ukraine, they are stepping up attacks on Ukraine ⁠as well as hybrid acts in Europe,” the official said. “As always, Nato remains vigilant and alert to ⁠the variety of threats we face. At this time, we ​see no imminent threat ‌of attack,” the official ‌said, adding: “We continue to stand with Ukraine. And Nato continues ‌to work around the clock to keep our one billion people safe.” Continue reading...

Ukraine wants ⁠to bring forward part of ⁠a European ⁠Union ​loan earmarked for next year ⁠to help cover a $27bn budget ⁠deficit this year, ​said its defence ‌minister, Yevhenii Khmara. data.title: Parasomnia review – sleep-schedule horror conjures up a succubus on the loose in waking nightmare
data.description: Debut director James Ross II shows promise in this gore fest, but the fear factor suffers from an overly complex plot Sleep has been part of the horror genre repertoire since The Cabinet of Dr Caligari, and the anxieties around it are spiking as the “ sleep economy ” becomes a thing. This ambitiously structured gore fest about a woman suffering from waking nightmares comes with an all-black cast, but race isn’t a central preoccupation here. Instead, as night terrors burst the banks into reality, debut director James Ross II concentrates on maintaining an appropriately scrambled and claustrophobic experience – perhaps to the detriment of the fear factor. On her 15th birthday, Riley (Jasmine Mathews) is paralysed in a waking/sleep state at her foster home, able to observe but powerless to intervene to stop a care worker going berserk. Since this massacre, Riley keeps a strict sleep protocol as an adult, making sure anyone under the same roof drops off before her, which apparently protects them from the malevolent presence invading her nights. Old foster home pal David (Stephen Barrington) accepts an invitation to the house where Riley’s dad murdered her mum, but gets the willies when a pallid demon begins manifesting in the small hours. It turns out that Riley’s boyfriend, Cam (RJ Brown), has been lax in letting her fall asleep before him – and now her resident succubus is on the loose again. Continue reading...

data.title: Bel review – the powerful life force and haunting absence of a traumatised singer-songwriter
data.description: Beldina Odenyo alchemised the pain of exile, loss and racism into music as Heir of the Cursed before her death in 2021, as this attentive tribute explores Instead of an artist in a booth, a lone amplifier plays the music of singer-songwriter Beldina Odenyo for a cluster of microphones to pick up during the posthumous recording of her debut album. It is a haunting encapsulation of the absence and presence at the heart of Louise Lockwood’s documentary, which makes a commendably thorough exploration of the mental illness that led to Odenyo killing herself in November 2021, and its roots: exile, loss and racism. Performing under the moniker Heir of the Cursed, a translation of the Tetela name of assassinated Congolese leader Patrice Lumumba , Odenyo was on the verge of bigger recognition at the end of 2021 after a successful performance at Edinburgh’s Usher Hall. But hemmed in by successive Covid lockdowns, the 31-year-old is clearly unwell in a discomfiting backstage interview. Squirming, monosyllabic, she seems to be regressing to the non-verbal state of shock in which she arrived in Dumfriesshire from Kenya as a young child. Continue reading...

data.title: Switzy by Emma Cline review – this Booker-listed account of a man’s last days is profoundly moving
data.description: Struggling with Alzheimer’s, the central character sets out on his final journey to a euthanasia clinic The word “Alzheimer’s” never appears in Switzy, Emma Cline’s third novel, which arrives pre-endorsed as a Booker prize longlistee. But we can be certain that it is the disease afflicting its central character, David Hastings – certain in a way he finds it increasingly hard to be about anything. When the novel begins, David and his assistant Cody are aboard a private jet flying from his home in the US to the UK. Landing at London City airport (which the book, experiencing its own senior moment, situates in the countryside), they visit David’s daughter and her family before travelling on to Zurich (hence “Switzy”). One more appointment, a catchup with an old boarding school roommate called Tom, awaits just over the French border, after which David will be euthanised at a facility resembling Dignitas. Continue reading...

data.title: The Future Starts With Us by Gordon Brown review – the ex-PM’s recipe for beating populism
data.description: Global crises are tightly linked to how we treat each other at the local level, argues this optimistic book In times of crisis, there is one person to whom the left still turns for guidance. More than a decade and a half after leaving government, Gordon Brown has mellowed into the Labour party’s favourite wise elder; one who has never disappointed the faithful by going off to make a ton of money, remaining quietly committed to public service and deeply engaged with the world’s knottier problems. Having successfully led the global response to the financial crash of 2008, and advocated powerfully during the pandemic for global cooperation against the virus, he was never going to simply sit back and shrug as the world spiralled into conflict and chaos under Donald Trump. data.title: ‘Who would dare take on Elizabeth Jane Howard’s fans?’ Louisa Young on reviving the Cazalet Chronicles
data.description: The author’s new trilogy continues her aunt’s beloved family saga. What would happen next to the sprawling cast of characters ... and could she pull it off? In the late 1980s Elizabeth Jane Howard was wondering what to write next. Jane, as she was always known, was at that time the author of seven novels. Her debut, The Beautiful Visit, had won the John Llewellyn Rhys prize in 1951 when she was 28 years old and The Long View (1956) was one of the first novels written with reverse chronology. Her talent was somewhat overshadowed in a tawdry world by her drop-dead beauty and by her having briefly been an actor (and by the famous lovers and husbands she walked out on, including Sir Peter Scott, the ornithologist and conservationist, in 1946, and Kingsley Amis, who was then himself a famous novelist, in 1983). Stuck, she asked her stepson Martin Amis which of two projects she should go for: an updated version of Sense and Sensibility, or a family saga based on her own life? He said, do the family saga. Jane’s family project developed into the Cazalet Chronicles: five volumes in which she fictionalised her life’s experience, divided between three young female cousins, Polly, Clary and Louise, and a cast of 52 more named characters, set between London and a grandparental family home in Sussex. Continue reading...

data.title: The Waterboys review – Steve Earle joins a gloriously unruly return to Fisherman’s Blues
data.description: OVO Hydro, Glasgow The Nashville singer-songwriter is among the guests joining Mike Scott for a sprawling, exuberant revue that finds new life in the Waterboys’ rootsy past This is strange. A Waterboys gig, but something else, too: the first night of the Fisherman’s Blues Revue. Which is what, exactly? Inspired by the Rolling Thunder Revue, the wild tour in which Bob Dylan performed alongside a troupe of guest stars, Mike Scott’s version is a way of digging into the rootsy music he and his band were making in the mid-1980s, some of which emerged on the classic Fisherman’s Blues. The aim of this show is not a faithful play-through of that album, which Scott has said he would find dull, but a “reigniting” of its spirit. The fire is lit with an opening half-hour of favourites: A Girl Called Johnny is notable for the legs-akimbo keytar heroics of Brother Paul Brown. Scott gives him a shout-out and promises “a few other miscreants and villains yet to join us”. Chief among them is Steve Earle, who takes the stage after the interval. Ursine and magnetic, the mandolin looks like a toy in his hands as he sings Copperhead Road and others from his songbook. It feels, for a while, like a Steve Earle set dropped into a Waterboys gig, rather than a blending of the two. The wonderful exception is And a Bang on the Ear, Scott’s fond chronicle of lost loves. Reworked as a duet, Earle contributes new verses that seem to refer to his own romances: “Sandy was just 18 when I took her for my wife/I believed we’d be together all the seasons of my life”. It works beautifully. Not everything does. The show is too long, pushing three hours including the interval, and the room is too big. The Stolen Child, that shivery setting of a Yeats poem, is not heard to advantage in an arena. Yet there is an exuberance and intensity in the performances, especially the playing of fiddler Steve Wickham – veteran of Fisherman’s Blues – which threatens to tip over into transcendence. A closing Will the Circle Be Unbroken sends the audience out into the night having experienced something better than nostalgia: artists weaving a new tapestry from the bright threads of their past. • At the 3Arena, Dublin , 5 September and the O2, London , 12 September Continue reading...

data.title: Squash salad and chocolate mousse: Dean Parker’s recipes for early autumn
data.description: Celebrate the flavours of the coming season via this rewarding salad and rich dessert to share As the days start to shorten and the temperature drops (finally!), the produce becomes richer, sweeter and more comforting, and the onset of autumn is a time of year that naturally brings people together around the table, which is something I’ve always loved about food. At the restaurant, we try to let the ingredients do the talking, and we work closely with growers and producers to make the most of whatever’s in season. Today’s recipes celebrate some of my favourite seasonal flavours: the salad is simple but deeply satisfying, balancing sweet roast squash with bitter greens and a punchy black olive tapenade. For dessert, meanwhile, chocolate mousse with poached fruit is my idea of autumn in a bowl, not least because quince has a beautiful, floral character that develops as it cooks, and pairs perfectly with dark chocolate and the nutty richness of browned butter. The creme fraiche adds freshness and balance, and brings everything together. Both dishes are rooted in the philosophy that guides my cooking: celebrate the season, respect great ingredients and create food that encourages people to slow down and enjoy each other’s company. Continue reading...

data.title: É preciso uma proteção adequada para as mulheres apostadoras

data.title: O que comer para dormir bem? Como seus hábitos alimentares afetam o sono
data.description: Todo mundo que já exagerou no jantar sabe que o que comemos tem influência na qualidade do sono . Mas ela pode ser maior do que se pensava, segundo estudos recentes que se debruçaram sobre o tema. Um artigo publicado em julho no Journal of Internal Medicine encontrou associação entre maior diversidade da microbiota intestinal e melhor qualidade do sono. A investigação indica que ingerir cápsulas com bactérias benéficas reduziu em 13,9% os sintomas de insônia crônica com apenas um mês de tratamento contínuo. Leia mais (08/30/2026 - 17h00)
data.translatedTitle: What to eat to sleep well? How Your Eating Habits Affect Sleep
data.translatedDescription: Everyone who has ever overindulged at dinner knows that what we eat has an influence on the quality of our sleep. But it may be greater than previously thought, according to recent studies that have looked into the topic. An article published in July in the Journal of Internal Medicine found an association between greater intestinal microbiota diversity and better sleep quality. Research indicates that ingesting capsules with beneficial bacteria reduced symptoms of chronic insomnia by 13.9% after just one month of continuous treatment. Read more (08/30/2026 - 5pm)

data.title: Erik Esbjörnsson: Vådligt flygstunt ses som patriotisk gest i Sydafrika
data.description: Debatten rasar i flygkretsar efter att två passagerarflygplan i helgen flög farligt nära en fullsatt rugbyarena i Kapstaden. Men i Sydafrika sluter man upp i stolthet bakom piloterna och flygbolaget – som i publikens ögon genomförde en patriotisk gest förankrad i nationens största idrottsögonblick.
data.translatedTitle: Erik Esbjörnsson: Violent aerial stunts are seen as a patriotic gesture in South Africa
data.translatedDescription: Debate is raging in aviation circles after two passenger jets flew dangerously close to a packed rugby stadium in Cape Town at the weekend. But in South Africa, they rally behind the pilots and the airline - who, in the eyes of the public, carried out a patriotic gesture anchored in the nation's greatest sporting moment.

data.title: Svenska hjälpen stoppades – ingen tog över: ”Barn har dött”
data.description: Det Sida-finansierade programmet i södra Etiopien drogs in till följd av regeringens nya försiktighetsprincip – utan att någon ersättare var på plats. Nu uppger lokala ledare att barn har dött. ”Det är extremt olyckligt. Men att barn dör till följd av bristande humanitära resurser är tyvärr en tragisk verklighet i många kriser i världen”, skriver Bilan Osman Jama på Sida.
data.translatedTitle: Swedish aid was stopped - no one took over: "Children have died"
data.translatedDescription: The Sida-financed program in southern Ethiopia was withdrawn as a result of the government's new precautionary principle - without a replacement in place. Now local leaders say children have died. "It is extremely unfortunate. But the fact that children die as a result of a lack of humanitarian resources is unfortunately a tragic reality in many crises in the world," writes Bilan Osman Jama on Sida.

data.title: Betyg utan stress: Expertens råd till föräldrar

data.translatedTitle: Grades without stress: The expert's advice for parents
data.translatedDescription: The school term is in full swing and the homework will soon start piling up. Talking about grades can arouse many emotions, both in children and parents. - Focus on learning, says behavioral scientist Petra Krantz Lindgren, who gives advice on how to motivate to study.

data.title: VM-hoppet lever för Sverige: ”Chanserna är större nu”
data.description: En vinst och en förlust under första kvalfönstret i andra rundan av VM-kvalet i basket för Sverige. Nu väntar ytterligare fyra matcher i resan mot VM – men då utan storstjärnan Pelle Larsson. – Alla kommer behöva steppa upp, säger Ludvig Håkanson.
data.translatedTitle: The World Cup hopes are alive for Sweden: "The chances are greater now"
data.translatedDescription: A win and a loss during the first qualifying window in the second round of the World Cup qualifiers in basketball for Sweden. Now four more games await in the journey to the World Cup - but then without superstar Pelle Larsson. - Everyone will have to step up, says Ludvig Håkanson.

data.title: Emma Bouvin: Ingen vill ha krig och ingen vill sluta fred
data.description: För första gången på flera veckor har USA attackerat Iran, som svarade med missiler mot Jordanien och Förenade arabemiraten. Mycket talar för att detta är det nya normala – ett krig som pågår lågintensivt för att flamma upp med jämna mellanrum.
data.translatedTitle: Emma Bouvin: Nobody wants war and nobody wants to make peace
data.translatedDescription: For the first time in weeks, the US has attacked Iran, which responded with missiles at Jordan and the United Arab Emirates. There are many indications that this is the new normal – a war that is waged at low intensity only to flare up at regular intervals.

data.title: I Aya Kanbars ”Kalven” blir begäret en form av ensamhet
data.description: I sin tredje diktsamling har den 22-åriga poeten blivit stramare i formen, men skriver fortfarande med en närmast eruptiv språklig kraft, tycker Gabriel Itkes-Sznap.
data.translatedTitle: In Aya Kanbar's "The Calf", desire becomes a form of loneliness
data.translatedDescription: In his third collection of poems, the 22-year-old poet has become stricter in form, but still writes with an almost eruptive linguistic power, Gabriel Itkes-Sznap thinks.

data.title: Kärnkraftsbolag får backning på årsredovisning

data.translatedTitle: Nuclear power companies get backing on annual report
data.translatedDescription: Blykalla - which is seeking billions in support from the state to build new nuclear power reactors - receives backing on its annual report. The Swedish Companies Registration Office has given the company an injunction on several points. Blykalla does not think the injunction will affect the applications with the government.

data.title: Firar sig ned med rep – letar överlevande i tunneln i Nepal
data.description: Fler än 100 arbetare vid vattenkraftverk befaras vara fast i tunnlar efter flodvågen i Himalaya. Räddningsarbetare har firat ned sig i en tunnel för att leta efter överlevande. De har ropat utan att få svar, enligt Nepals premiärministers kontor.
data.translatedTitle: Climbing down with rope - looking for survivors in the tunnel in Nepal
data.translatedDescription: More than 100 hydroelectric power plant workers are feared trapped in tunnels after the Himalayan tidal wave. Rescue workers have descended into a tunnel to search for survivors. They have been calling out without getting a response, according to Nepal's prime minister's office.

data.title: Vesna Prekopic: Jo, SVT – ni normaliserar en extrem åsikt i ”Gift vid första ögonkastet”
data.description: Att vänta i flera avsnitt med att problematisera det toxiska beteendet i ”GVFÖ” är inte bara sensationslystet – det bidrar till att göra psykiskt våld till underhållning, skriver Vesna Prekopic.
data.translatedTitle: Vesna Prekopic: Yes, SVT - you normalize an extreme opinion in "Married at First Sight"
data.translatedDescription: Waiting for several episodes to problematize the toxic behavior in "GVFÖ" is not just sensationalism - it contributes to turning psychological violence into entertainment, writes Vesna Prekopic.

data.title: Forskare: Bygg bättre för att skydda våra hjärnor
data.description: När artificiell intelligens tar över rutinjobben ställs helt nya krav på mänsklig kreativitet och problemlösning. Men dagens kontor och städer dränerar oss på energi. Enligt neuroarkitekturforskaren Cleo Valentine krävs nu en revolution i hur vi bygger för att skydda vårt allra viktigaste kapital – vår hjärnhälsa.
data.translatedTitle: Scientists: Build better to protect our brains
data.translatedDescription: When artificial intelligence takes over routine jobs, completely new demands are placed on human creativity and problem solving. But today's offices and cities drain us of energy. According to neuroarchitecture researcher Cleo Valentine, a revolution in the way we build is now required to protect our most important capital – our brain health.

data.title: Örebropartiet tredubblar stödet i Örebro län – har chans på riksdagen
data.description: En ny opinionsmätning från Novus och Nerikes Allehanda indikerar att Sverige kan få ett nytt riksdagsparti: Örebropartiet (ÖP). Det nationalistiska populistpartiet ökar kraftigt och har nu 15 procents stöd i regionvalet. Om ÖP även i riksdagsvalet samlar minst 12 procent i valkretsen Örebro län väljs partiledaren Markus Allard in i riksdagen.
data.translatedTitle: The Örebro Party triples its support in Örebro County - has a chance in the Riksdag
data.translatedDescription: A new opinion poll from Novus and Nerikes Allehanda indicates that Sweden may get a new Riksdag party: the Örebro Party (ÖP). The nationalist populist party is increasing strongly and now has 15 percent support in the regional election. If the ÖP collects at least 12 percent in the constituency Örebro län in the parliamentary election as well, the party leader Markus Allard will be elected to the Riksdag.

data.title: Tomas Ramberg: Centerns strategi är bingo för Dadgostar
data.description: Spekulationerna om en mittenregering är den bästa hjälp Nooshi Dadgostar kan få i valets slutspurt. Vänsterpartiets chans är att många S-väljare vill dra Magdalena Andersson vänsterut och därför lägger sin röst på V. Samtidigt lättar trycket på Dadgostar i regeringsfrågan.
data.translatedTitle: Tomas Ramberg: The center's strategy is bingo for Dadgostar
data.translatedDescription: Speculation about a centrist government is the best help Nooshi Dadgostar can get in the run-up to the election. The left party's chance is that many S-voters want to pull Magdalena Andersson to the left and therefore vote for V. At the same time, the pressure on Dadgostar in the government issue eases.

data.title: Fartigt och underhållande om fatala misstag
data.description: Misslyckandet är triumfens granne. Peter Englund synar de stora olyckorna och gigantiska krascherna. Konstnärliga och industriella. Mänskliga fiaskon som borde ha kunnat undvikas. Victor Malm läser en god och underhållande essäbok.
data.translatedTitle: Fast-paced and entertaining about fatal mistakes
data.translatedDescription: Failure is the neighbor of triumph. Peter Englund sees the big accidents and gigantic crashes. Artistic and industrial. Human failures that should have been avoidable. Victor Malm reads a good and entertaining book of essays.

data.title: Så blev valaffischerna mer tradition än politik: ”Som sill på midsommar”
data.description: Den 16 augusti började partierna affischera inför valet. DN tar en titt i valaffischens historia, från klasskamp till försök att fånga alla väljare samtidigt. – Valaffischerna har gått från ideologi till varumärkesbyggande, säger medie- och kommunikationsforskaren Bengt Johansson, som även kallar sig för propagandainspektör.
data.translatedTitle: This is how the election posters became more tradition than politics: "Like herring at midsummer"
data.translatedDescription: On August 16, the parties began to advertise before the election. DN takes a look at the history of the election poster, from class struggle to attempts to capture all voters at the same time. - The election posters have gone from ideology to branding, says media and communication researcher Bengt Johansson, who also calls himself a propaganda inspector.

data.title: Nytt digitalt arkiv gör historiska valaffischer tillgängliga för alla
data.description: Budskapen har blivit hoppfullare och leendena fler. Svenska valaffischer har ändrat färg, form och retorik genom åren. Nu öppnar Propagandaindex, ett digitalt arkiv där alla som vill kan bläddra bland historiska affischer. DN är med på satsningen. – Det här är en historisk skatt, säger chefredaktör Peter Wolodarski.
data.translatedTitle: New digital archive makes historic election posters accessible to everyone
data.translatedDescription: The messages have become more hopeful and the smiles more numerous. Swedish election posters have changed color, shape and rhetoric over the years. Propaganda Index is now open, a digital archive where anyone who wants to can browse historical posters. DN is involved in the investment. - This is a historical treasure, says editor-in-chief Peter Wolodarski.

data.title: Stefan Jonsson: Här är satsningarna som krävs i kulturpolitiken
data.description: Satsningar på kulturen skulle blåsa in som en frisk vind i en politik som låst sig i kortsynt syndabockstänkande. Kanske rent av substans och mening åt den frihet, välfärd och gemenskap som politikerna talar om, skriver Stefan Jonsson.
data.translatedTitle: Stefan Jonsson: Here are the investments required in cultural policy
data.translatedDescription: Investments in culture would blow in like a fresh wind in a policy locked in short-sighted scapegoat thinking. Perhaps purely in terms of substance and meaning to the freedom, welfare and community that the politicians talk about, writes Stefan Jonsson.

data.translatedDescription: Zebastian Modin made his Paralympic debut in cross-country skiing back in 2010 – aged 15. Now, 16 years later, the biggest focus is on biathlon. - I need something new, he says.

data.description: När stenhårda Ebba Busch började prata om att politiken behövde mer ”hjärta”. tänkte jag: lycka till Men även det lappkastet klarade Sveriges skickligaste politiker.
data.translatedTitle: Alex Schulman: Ebba Busch's transformation from ice queen to Mother Teresa is genius
data.translatedDescription: When stubborn Ebba Busch started talking about politics needing more "heart". I thought: good luck But Sweden's most skilled politician also managed that patchwork.

data.translatedDescription: Sweden Democrat Richard Jomshof detests Islam. His new book is about how Sweden is to be freed from it.

data.title: Dadgostars uppmaning till missnöjda S-väljare: ”Skicka en signal”
data.description: GÖTEBORG. Vänsterpartiets Nooshi Dadgostar planerar att styra med Socialdemokraterna, som säger att V inte är ett regeringsdugligt parti. Nu uppmanar Dadgostar S-väljare att ge dem en chans. – Partiledningen i Socialdemokraterna har legat långt ut på högerkanten om man jämför med gräsrötterna, säger V-ledaren.
data.translatedTitle: Dadgostar's appeal to dissatisfied S voters: "Send a signal"
data.translatedDescription: GOTHENBURG. The Left Party's Nooshi Dadgostar plans to govern with the Social Democrats, who say V is not a government-capable party. Now Dadgostar is urging S voters to give them a chance. - The party leadership in the Social Democrats has been far to the right if you compare it to the grassroots, says the V leader.

data.title: Ledare: Moderaterna brukade vara seriösa i finanspolitiken – vad har hänt?
data.description: Sverige har exceptionellt starka statsfinanser. Det är tack vare att två statsbärande partier satt ramarna – för sig själva, varandra och andra. Nu seglar Moderaterna iväg.
data.translatedTitle: Leader: The moderates used to be serious about fiscal policy - what has happened?
data.translatedDescription: Sweden has exceptionally strong public finances. It is thanks to two state-bearing parties setting the framework – for themselves, each other and others. Now the Moderates are sailing away.

data.title: Insändare. Stäng inte ute svenskar i världen från valet
data.description: INSÄNDARE. Det är orimligt att man som svensk medborgare bosatt utomlands ändå kan nekas att få delta i höstens val. I stället för att låta tidigare folkbokföring vara avgörande för rösträtt bör en möjlighet införas för svenska medborgare som aldrig bott i Sverige att rösta, skriver utlandssvenskan Alicia Alserholm.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Do not exclude Swedes in the world from the election
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. It is unreasonable that as a Swedish citizen living abroad, you can still be denied the right to participate in the autumn elections. Instead of letting previous population registration be decisive for the right to vote, an opportunity should be introduced for Swedish citizens who have never lived in Sweden to vote, writes expatriate Swede Alicia Alserholm.

data.title: Uppgifter: USA har genomfört nya attacker mot Iran
data.description: USA:s president Donald Trump hävdar att den iranska oljeön Kharg ”sprängs i bitar”. Till inlägget på sociala medier delar han en AI-video på en kraftig explosion. Utspelet kommer i samband med att USA genomfört nya attacker mot Iran och revolutionsgardet har svarat med egna attacker i Jordanien.
data.translatedTitle: Details: The US has carried out new attacks against Iran
data.translatedDescription: US President Donald Trump claims that the Iranian oil island of Kharg is "being blown to pieces". To accompany the social media post, he shares an AI video of a powerful explosion. The development comes in connection with the USA carrying out new attacks against Iran and the Revolutionary Guards have responded with their own attacks in Jordan.

data.title: 30 augusti: Missa inte dagens nyheter
data.description: Färja har kapsejsat utanför Cypern, skjutning på rejv i Schweiz och så kan en regering se ut efter valet – här är nyheterna du inte får missa från dagen.
data.translatedTitle: August 30: Don't miss today's news
data.translatedDescription: A ferry has capsized off Cyprus, shooting at a reef in Switzerland and this is what a government might look like after the election - here are the news you can't miss from the day.

data.title: Michael Winiarski: Trumpfamiljen köpte paradisområde av kokainsmugglare
data.description: I månader har tusentals albaner demonstrerat mot Trumpfamiljens planer på att bygga lyxbostäder på två orörda naturreservat. Premiärminister Edi Rama vägrar att backa från det omstridda miljardprojektet, trots att det visat sig att en kokainsmugglare har sålt marken till Donald Trumps svärson.
data.translatedTitle: Michael Winiarski: Trump family bought paradise area from cocaine smugglers
data.translatedDescription: For months, thousands of Albanians have demonstrated against the Trump family's plans to build luxury homes on two pristine nature reserves. Prime Minister Edi Rama refuses to back down from the controversial multi-billion dollar project, even though it has emerged that a cocaine smuggler has sold the land to Donald Trump's son-in-law.

data.title: Mystisk konstkupp – stal renässansverk för miljoner
data.description: Ännu saknas spår efter den fräcka konstkuppen på Sicilien tidigare i augusti. På tre minuter lyckades tjuvarna komma över flera renässansverk värda mångmiljonbelopp.
data.translatedTitle: Mysterious art coup - stolen renaissance work worth millions
data.translatedDescription: There is still no trace of the brazen art coup in Sicily earlier in August. In three minutes, the thieves managed to come across several Renaissance works worth many millions.

data.title: Kan ett meningsfullt liv påverka hälsan?
data.description: Vad får oss att känna att livet hänger ihop och är värt att leva? Frågan har länge hört hemma i filosofin och religionen. Nu kliver den in på folkhälsoområdet, där Folkhälsomyndigheten undersöker hur mening, sammanhang och tillhörighet hänger ihop med vår hälsa. Men alla är inte övertygade om att detta är en bra idé.
data.translatedTitle: Can a meaningful life affect health?
data.translatedDescription: What makes us feel that life is connected and worth living? The question has long belonged in philosophy and religion. Now it steps into the area of ​​public health, where the Public Health Agency investigates how meaning, context and belonging are connected to our health. But not everyone is convinced that this is a good idea.

data.title: Bengt Ohlsson: Torsten Ehrenmark snuddade fjäderlätt vid sina egna smärtpunkter
data.description: I serien ”Benkes tidsmaskin” bläddrar författaren och skribenten Bengt Ohlsson i DN:s hundraåriga arkiv i jakt på gårdagens nyheter. Den här veckan landar han i Torsten Ehrenmarks kåserier.
data.translatedTitle: Bengt Ohlsson: Torsten Ehrenmark touched his own pain points with ease
data.translatedDescription: In the series "Benke's time machine", author Bengt Ohlsson browses DN's century-old archive in search of yesterday's news. This week he lands in Torsten Ehrenmark's house series.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Alla tänker på den, få litar på den – varför pratar ingen om pensionen?”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Pensionssystemet blir allt krångligare, och de egna valen får allt större betydelse för den framtida ekonomin. Men allt färre vill ta det stora ansvaret, och många känner att reglerna är obegripliga. Ändå lyser frågan med sin frånvaro i valdebatten – trots att mer än varannan väljare vill höra mer, skriver Shoka Åhrman, pensionsbolaget SPP.
data.translatedTitle: DN Debate. "Everyone thinks about it, few trust it - why does no one talk about the pension?"
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE. The pension system is becoming more and more complicated, and one's own choices are becoming more and more important for the future economy. But fewer and fewer want to take on the big responsibility, and many feel that the rules are incomprehensible. Nevertheless, the issue shines with its absence in the election debate - despite the fact that more than every second voter wants to hear more, writes Shoka Åhrman, pension company SPP.

data.title: Bildspel: Så stor är förödelsen – husen som begravts i leran i Nepal
data.description: Bilden av den enorma förödelsen i Nepal klarnar allt mer. Förutom alla dödade och skadade har bostadshus, broar och vägar spolats bort, begravts i lera eller översvämmats. På sina håll har människor börjat återvända för att se vad som kan räddas.
data.translatedTitle: Slideshow: That's how big the devastation is - the houses buried in the mud in Nepal
data.translatedDescription: The picture of the enormous devastation in Nepal is becoming clearer. In addition to all the dead and injured, residential buildings, bridges and roads have been washed away, buried in mud or flooded. In some places, people have started to return to see what can be saved.

data.title: Sverige pressade Frankrike – föll i slutminuterna
data.description: Sverige pressade OS-tvåan Frankrike länge i VM-kvalet – men orkade inte hela vägen. I slutminuterna var bortalaget starkare och vann till slut med 15 poäng. – Till slut hade vi inte energin, men jag är väldigt stolt över laget, säger Ludvig Håkanson.
data.translatedTitle: Sweden pressured France - fell in the final minutes
data.translatedDescription: Sweden pressured Olympic runner-up France for a long time in the World Cup qualifiers - but couldn't make it all the way. In the final minutes, the away team was stronger and eventually won by 15 points. - In the end we didn't have the energy, but I'm very proud of the team, says Ludvig Håkanson.

data.title: En bråkdel av jägarnas omstridda vapen har lämnats in
data.description: Vapnet AR-15:s plats i svensk jakt har varit en politisk hetpotatis. I snart ett år har de 7 000 som har jaktlicens för vapnet frivilligt kunnat lämna in geväret. Men siffror från myndigheter visar att de flesta är kvar i jägarnas händer.
data.translatedTitle: A fraction of the hunters' disputed weapons have been handed in
data.translatedDescription: The weapon AR-15's place in Swedish hunting has been a political hot potato. For almost a year, the 7,000 who have a hunting license for the weapon have been able to voluntarily hand in the rifle. But figures from authorities show that most remain in the hands of hunters.

data.title: ”Hela Tyskland ska vakna och vi ska bli normala människor igen”
data.description: QUEDLINBURG. På DDR-tillverkade mopeder kör den historiska valrörelsen genom Tyskland. För första gången sedan andra världskriget kan ett högerextremt parti, AFD, bilda delstatsregering. Valet i Sachsen-Anhalt kan förändra Tyskland – och därmed Europa.
data.translatedTitle: "All of Germany will wake up and we will become normal people again"
data.translatedDescription: QUEDLINBURG. On GDR-made mopeds, the historic election campaign drives through Germany. For the first time since the Second World War, a far-right party, AFD, can form a state government. The election in Saxony-Anhalt could change Germany – and thus Europe.

data.title: Mittbacken hjälte för Blåvitt i derbyt
data.description: I söndagens andra fotbollsallsvenska derby stod IFK Göteborg som vinnare efter att Hjörtur Hermannsson gjort matchens enda mål mot Örgryte.
data.translatedTitle: Center back hero for Blåvitt in the derby
data.translatedDescription: In Sunday's second Allsvenskan football derby, IFK Göteborg were the winners after Hjörtur Hermannsson scored the only goal of the match against Örgryte.

data.title: Bakslag för Hammarby – men skyttekungen blir kvar
data.description: Hammarbys Paulos Abraham ser trots bud från utlandet ut att bli kvar i klubben för att jaga ett SM-guld. Den uppgiften blir något svårare efter derbyförlusten mot AIK. – Man jag tror inte guldstriden är förlorad, säger han.
data.translatedTitle: Setback for Hammarby - but the top scorer remains
data.translatedDescription: Despite offers from abroad, Hammarby's Paulos Abraham looks set to remain at the club to chase a SM gold. That task becomes somewhat more difficult after the derby loss against AIK. - Man, I don't think the battle for gold is lost, he says.

data.title: Hundratals oidentifierade kroppar begravs i skogen i Nepal
data.description: Hundratals oidentifierade kroppar begravs nu i en skog långt ifrån katastrofområdet i Nepal. – Vi har inget annat val, säger distriktschef Ganesh Arya. Samtidigt pågår ett febrilt arbete med att försöka rädda överlevande.
data.translatedTitle: Hundreds of unidentified bodies are buried in the forest in Nepal
data.translatedDescription: Hundreds of unidentified bodies are now buried in a forest far from the disaster area in Nepal. - We have no other choice, says district manager Ganesh Arya. At the same time, feverish work is underway to try to save survivors.

data.title: Malins axel frös till: ”Vissa nätter orkar jag bara inte mer”
data.description: Obeskrivlig smärta, uppriven sömn och problem med de lättaste av vardagssysslor. När Malin Mauritsen, 51, fick diagnosen frozen shoulder insåg hon hur få svar det fanns om sjukdomen, som främst drabbar kvinnor i medelåldern. – Vissa nätter känner man bara att nu orkar jag bara inte mer, säger hon.
data.translatedTitle: Malin's shoulder froze: "Some nights I just can't take it anymore"
data.translatedDescription: Indescribable pain, disturbed sleep and problems with the simplest of everyday tasks. When Malin Mauritsen, 51, was diagnosed with frozen shoulder, she realized how few answers there were about the disease, which mainly affects middle-aged women. - Some nights you just feel that now I just can't take it anymore, she says.

data.title: Norsk 14-åring stal buss – ville plocka upp passagerare
data.description: I fredags stoppades en stadsbuss på E18 utanför Oslo. I förarsätet satt en 14-årig pojke – som stulit sin fjärde buss.
data.translatedTitle: Norwegian 14-year-old stole bus - wanted to pick up passengers
data.translatedDescription: Last Friday, a city bus was stopped on E18 outside Oslo. In the driver's seat was a 14-year-old boy — who stole his fourth bus.

data.title: Så gör du när en anhörig behöver hjälp med ekonomin
data.description: Mycket kan gå fel i kontakten med banker och myndigheter när äldre eller andra anhöriga behöver hjälp, det vittnar både DN-läsare och olika aktörer om. Här är tipsen för att undvika de vanligaste fällorna.
data.translatedTitle: This is what you do when a relative needs help with finances
data.translatedDescription: A lot can go wrong in contact with banks and authorities when the elderly or other relatives need help, both DN readers and various actors attest to that. Here are tips to avoid the most common traps.

data.title: Massflykt från städerna i öster när drönarhotet kryper närmre
data.description: LOZOVA. Vem som helst kan bli måltavla för Rysslands pilotstyrda drönare. Nu når de allt längre – och tvingar de civila att fly västerut. – Attackerna har blivit mycket värre. Till slut kunde vi inte längre gå ut, säger Dmytro Makarov, 23 som lämnat sin hemstad Kramatorsk.
data.translatedTitle: Mass flight from the cities in the east as the drone threat creeps closer
data.translatedDescription: LOZOVA. Anyone can be a target of Russia's pilot-controlled drones. Now they reach further and further - and force the civilians to flee west. - The attacks have become much worse. In the end, we could no longer go out, says Dmytro Makarov, 23, who left his hometown of Kramatorsk.

data.title: Island: EU-samtal utesluts under mandatperiod
data.description: Island säger nej till EU-förhandlingar i landets folkomröstning. Närmare 53 procent röstade emot medlemskap. Statsminister Kristrún Frostadóttir, som vill gå med i EU, säger att resultatet ”inte är ett bakslag” utan ”en seger för demokratin”.
data.translatedTitle: Iceland: EU talks are excluded during term of office
data.translatedDescription: Iceland says no to EU negotiations in the country's referendum. Close to 53 percent voted against membership. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir, who wants to join the EU, says the result is "not a setback" but "a victory for democracy".

data.title: AIK:s tränare stolt över ”kidsen” efter ny derbyseger
data.description: AIK:s säsong har varit full av motgångar – ändå är laget med och fajtas långt upp i fotbollsallsvenskan. Mot Hammarby tog laget en ny derbyseger, 3–2, och åter var det de unga och nya som klev fram. – Jag kan inte vara annat än en stolt coach för de här ”kidsen” säger AIK:s tränare José Riveiro.
data.translatedTitle: AIK's coach proud of the "kids" after another derby victory
data.translatedDescription: AIK's season has been full of setbacks - yet the team is in and fighting far up in the football Allsvenskan. Against Hammarby, the team took another derby victory, 3–2, and again it was the young and new who stepped forward. - I can only be a proud coach for these "kids", says AIK's coach José Riveiro.

data.title: S-ledaren upprepar ”varning” om Liseberg och mat till gamla
data.description: En anmälan om billiga skolhyror i Göteborg har åter satt lagen om offentlig säljverksamhet i fokus. S-ledaren Magdalena Andersson menar att den riskerar både Liseberg och restauranger på äldreboenden. Ett utspel som avfärdas av Moderaterna.
data.translatedTitle: The S leader repeats "warning" about Liseberg and food for the elderly
data.translatedDescription: A notification about cheap school rents in Gothenburg has once again brought the law on public sales activities into focus. S leader Magdalena Andersson believes that it risks both Liseberg and restaurants in nursing homes. A move that is dismissed by the Moderates.

data.title: Målfoto avgjorde – Sverige hårsmån från dubbelseger
data.description: Finnkampen 2026 blev ett friidrottsdrama ända in på mållinjen. Alice Magnell Millán fixade segern till Sveriges damer, men på herrsidan blev det förlust – efter målfoto. – Sjukt surt, säger 1 500-meterslöparen Jonas Magnusson.
data.translatedTitle: Goal photo decided - Sweden narrowly missed a double victory
data.translatedDescription: Finnkampen 2026 became an athletics drama right up to the finish line. Alice Magnell Millán fixed the victory for Sweden's ladies, but on the men's side it was a loss - after a goal photo. - Very sad, says the 1,500 meter runner Jonas Magnusson.

data.title: Låt någon annan titta på ditt bajs – och lev längre
data.description: De svenskar som aktivt deltar i screening av tjock- och ändtarmscancer har en väsentligt lägre risk att dö av sjukdomen. Trots det väljer en tredjedel att inte skicka in något avföringsprov.
data.translatedTitle: Let someone else watch your poop – and live longer
data.translatedDescription: Swedes who actively participate in colon and rectal cancer screening have a significantly lower risk of dying from the disease. Despite that, a third choose not to submit a stool sample.

data.title: Jan Eklund: 10 fackböcker att se fram emot i höst
data.description: Bokhösten är som hetast i september och oktober. Mary Beard skriver om klassiker, Peter Englund granskar misslyckanden och Samar Yazbek undersöker våldet i Gaza. DN:s Jan Eklund listar 10 höstböcker att hålla koll på.
data.translatedTitle: Jan Eklund: 10 nonfiction books to look forward to this fall
data.translatedDescription: The beech autumn is at its hottest in September and October. Mary Beard writes about classics, Peter Englund examines failures and Samar Yazbek examines the violence in Gaza. DN's Jan Eklund lists 10 autumn books to keep an eye on.

data.title: Åkessons krav på Busch: ”Avfärda inviter”
data.description: SÖLVESBORG/STRÄNGNÄS. Efter att Jimmie Åkesson ställt frågan om man kan lita på Ebba Busch har de två Tidöledarna druckit kaffe ihop i Sölvesborg. – Jag står för ett annat ledarskap. Jag står för att lyfta fram styrkan i det blågula laget, säger Busch. Men Åkesson tycks inte helt övertygad – och ställer ett nytt krav på KD-ledaren.
data.translatedTitle: Åkesson's demands on Busch: "Reject invitations"
data.translatedDescription: SÖLVESBORG/STRÄNGNÄS. After Jimmie Åkesson asked the question if you can trust Ebba Busch, the two Tidö leaders drank coffee together in Sölvesborg. - I stand for a different kind of leadership. I stand to highlight the strength of the blue-yellow team, says Busch. But Åkesson does not seem completely convinced - and makes a new demand on the KD leader.

data.title: Rivaler och konflikter som präglat motorvärlden
data.description: Innovation, prestige och personliga vendettor har länge drivit motorvärlden framåt, men också splittrat den. Från Benz och Daimler till Ferrari och Lamborghini – här är berättelserna om konflikter i bilens historia.
data.translatedTitle: Rivals and conflicts that characterized the motor world
data.translatedDescription: Innovation, prestige and personal vendettas have long driven the motoring world forward, but also divided it. From Benz and Daimler to Ferrari and Lamborghini – here are the stories of conflicts in the history of the car.

data.title: Många saknas efter kapsejsad färja utanför Cypern
data.description: 18 personer saknas efter att en passagerarfärja med 267 personer ombord har kapsejsat utanför norra Cypern. Minst åtta personer har omkommit, enligt den turkisk-cypriotiske premiärministern. Flera besättningsmedlemmar och kaptenen har gripits.
data.translatedTitle: Many missing after ferry capsizes off Cyprus
data.translatedDescription: 18 people are missing after a passenger ferry with 267 people on board capsized off northern Cyprus. At least eight people have died, according to the Turkish Cypriot prime minister. Several crew members and the captain have been arrested.

data.translatedTitle: Two NATO skeptics in the lead in France - can affect cooperation with Sweden
data.translatedDescription: PARIS. Two NATO skeptics are leading the polls ahead of next year's presidential election in France. It raises questions about the cooperation on France's nuclear weapons that Emmanuel Macron has started in recent months with his allies – including Sweden.

data.title: Groei, groei, groei op G20-top voor ministers van Financiën?

Groei, groei, groei zal het mantra van de Amerikaanse voorzitter zijn en daarvoor moeten alle belemmeringen wijken. Maar wat is de G20 nog waard in deze verdeelde wereld?

data.translatedTitle: In this Rotterdam district, workers' houses gradually became expensive owner-occupied homes. Old and new residents now live there together: 'They don't even say hello'
data.translatedDescription: Two hundred years ago, the Rotterdam city council took the leap across the Nieuwe Maas to Feijenoord. The neighborhood has changed quite a bit since then. 'Veryupt' is a term that 'old' Feijenoorders sometimes use when they point to the houses with cargo bikes in front of the door.
